newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rye tops German intervention grain offers.
newsitem.headline: Rye tops German intervention grain offers.

text.p: Some 62,257 tonnes of grain were offered into German intervention stores last week, including 41,357 tonnes of rye, data from state board BLE showed on Monday.
Total grain volumes offered in the November-May 1996/97 intervention season lag those of last year.
By May 9, a total 1,112,680 tonnes had been offered, compared with 1,656,288 tonnes a year earlier.
After changes to green currency rates on May 6, the May buying-in price for all grains is at 248.61 marks/tonne, against 247.98 marks previously.
